newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt rules out change on budget tax powers.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt rules out change on budget tax powers.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government on Wednesday ruled out any change of special powers on fiscal policy in its 1997 budget despite renewed opposition from the centre-right Freedom Alliance.
"There's nothing new," government undersecretary Enrico Micheli told reporters when asked whether the government was working on new measures to meet the Freedom Alliance's demands.
Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi said earlier that the centre-right would not take part in the budget vote in the Senate (upper house) unless the government made concessions.

It vehemently opposes the government's plan to award itself special powers to set certain policy measures, including tax, without constant referral back to parliament and asked for the powers to be dropped on a planned new regional tax (IREP).

Parties in the ruling centre-left "Olive Tree" coalition on Tuesday offered what they said were concessions including a proposal to set up a commission of both houses of parliament to monitor how the cabinet used any such powers on fiscal policy.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's tough 1997 budget, designed to chop 62.5 trillion lire ($40.7 billion) off next year's budget, is due to be debated in the Senate from December 10 and to return to the lower Chamber of Deputies on December 16. ($1=1,533 lire)
